model: ATC1500 Fan Coil Controller - Application #3002 (Two-Pipe, On/Off Valve, Staged Fan, On/Off Damper)
applies_to: A two-pipe fan coil with one changeover heating/cooling valve (on/off), a multi-speed (staged) fan, two-wire PWM heating and an optional on/off fresh-air damper, run by the Johnson Controls ATC1500 with application #3002.
summary: Application #3002 is one of the fan coil applications for the Johnson Controls ATC1500 (4 UI, 2 BI, 2 BO, 4 RO, 3 CO) Advanced Terminal Unit Controller, which connects over BACnet MS/TP (it can also run N2 or Modbus). It drives a two-pipe fan coil with on/off valve control, a multi-speed (staged) fan, a two-wire PWM heating option and an optional on/off fresh-air damper. Points cover unit enable, occupancy and mode commands, network setpoint and network sensor overrides, fan, valve and damper status, PID tuning, fault detection flags and the controller's network settings.
notes: Objects from the BACnet and N2 bus points table on pages 49-67 of the application note (LIT-12013081).

All objects are analog values (AV) or multistate values (MV); physical inputs and outputs show up as MV/AV status points. Access W means the table marks the object Writeable; multistate states keep the 0-based numbers printed in the note.
For 6 multistate objects the note prints only the first states and then '...'; the full sets are in Metasys System Enumeration Sets (LIT-12011361).
This note prints some names with a second, user-interface label in brackets; the first name is used here and the bracketed label is in the description.
Application #3001 prints the same table except for the damper output: this one has MV 28042 OA Damper BO, MV 28044 Damper Polarity; #3001 has AV 28033 OA Damper PAO, MV 28043 Damper Polarity.
Units come from the range column: temperatures follow the controller Units setting (MV 28018, default SI so °C).

source.title: Advanced Terminal Unit Controller Application Note - Application #3002

integration.summary: Set the controller to BACnet MS/TP (FC Comm Mode Wired Field Bus) with an MS/TP address of 4-127, then enable the unit with Unit Enable Mode, drive occupancy through Occupancy Schedule and write Network Setpoint (Spt Source defaults to Network Input). Read unit status, effective occupancy, zone temperature and the fan state.

integration.enable: Unit Enable Mode (Shutdown or Enable, default Enable) turns the unit off or on. Effective occupancy follows Occupancy Override first, then the bypass timer, Occupancy Schedule and the occupancy sensor. System Mode Determination is the writable mode command (cool only, heat only, fan only and others). The note says a network mode command takes priority over the summer-winter changeover input.
integration.remote_sensors: With Spt Source at Network Input (the default) the zone setpoint comes from Network Setpoint (default 22 °C). Network Override Zone Temperature, Network Override Outdoor Air Temperature and Network Override Indoor Air Quality are writable network inputs; a network CO2 value takes priority over the local sensor, and summer-winter setpoint compensation only works with a reliable network outdoor air temperature.
setup: FC Comm Mode picks the field bus (Wired Field Bus for BACnet MS/TP, N2 or Modbus). MSTP Device Address is 4-127 and Device Object ID 0-4194302.
FCB Baud Rate defaults to Auto; Operating Baud Rate shows the rate in use and Communication Status the MS/TP state.
Units (MV 28018) selects IP or SI; the default is SI.
gotchas: BACnet IDs (AV 280xx / MV 280xx) are reused across the ATC applications but do not always mean the same point; map each application from its own list.
Occupancy Override and Occupancy Schedule read Not Set after a reset until written again; with both Not Set and no occupancy sensor the unit falls back to Default Occupancy (Occupied unless changed).
PID tuning, minimum on/off times and fault delays are commissioning values; don't write them cyclically.
